_about: Quantitative accuracy proof for the Valuein SEC fact dataset, computed nightly against production data. Re-derive with scripts/accuracy/accuracy_check.sql.

standardized_facts._definition: A filing is 'clean' when it passes every active error-severity accounting identity defined in identities.json.

legacy_pre_2010._note: Pre-2010 XBRL was optional; most pre-2010 filings have no facts and trivially pass every identity. Treat the modern_2010_onward number as the honest measurement.

trajectory._note: 10-iteration calibration history from production-data baseline to final. Every step traceable to a Pareto-leading identity and a real-world filer pattern.

iterations.change: baseline — out-of-the-box engine on first SP500 production run
tolerance bumps round 1 (bs_01, bs_02, bs_03, bs_04, is_04, is_05)
bs_05 + eps_02 polish, is_05 skip widened
demoted is_05 + bs_05 to warning (sector convention not math error)
demoted cf_01 to warning (bank/insurance reconciling-items convention)
demoted is_02 + sp_04 + sp_05 to warning (sector-specific structural cases)

top_remaining_pareto._note: filers reporting GP > Revenue — real data-extraction quality flag
industries without true COGS partition (consumer-staples distributors)
rare anti-dilution math errors in early XBRL filings

unstandardized_facts._definition: A fact with standard_concept = 'Other' is 'correctly unstandardized' if its raw XBRL tag is genuinely outside our 270-concept canonical catalog (non-us-gaap namespace, long-tail rare tag, or matched a documented disclosure-niche pattern).
unstandardized_facts._note: The 2.79% mapping-gap reflects 17 us-gaap aliases identified but not yet folded into the data-pipeline catalog. They'll land in the next pipeline release.

sources: Penman (2013) — Financial Statement Analysis and Security Valuation 5e
